## Current record

Use the Linear team **CRE Skills** (`CRE`) in workspace `mariourquia`.
This team holds current work for the `cre-skills` family.

Keep current scope, plans, owners, status, blockers, acceptance, and handoffs in Linear.
For families with multiple repositories, identify this repository with the label `repo:cre-skills-plugin`.

Keep code, ADRs, and runbooks as source evidence.
Link old plans and GitHub issues as historical evidence.
Do not file new work as a GitHub issue.
Use GitHub pull requests for source review and release evidence.

## How agents use it

The Linear MCP server (`https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`) is configured in Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. A harness can add a prefix to the tool names below. Where a tool takes a `team`, pass the team name (`CRE Skills`) or its ID. The key `CRE` is the prefix of the issue identifiers (`CRE-<n>`). Linear assigns them. A bare `#<n>` in a skill, for example `#42`, means the issue `CRE-<n>`. In this tracker it is never a pull request.

- Check the current owner and dependencies before work.
- **Create an issue**: `save_issue` with `team`, `title`, a Markdown `description`, and `labels`. On a new issue, `labels` is the whole label set. Give a new issue a plain title.
- **Update an issue**: `save_issue` with `id`. Change labels with `addLabels` and `removeLabels`. Do not send `labels` on an update, because it replaces the whole set. `state`, `assignee` (`"me"` is yourself), and `parentId` also go through `save_issue`.
- **Relations**: `blockedBy`, `blocks`, and `relatedTo` on `save_issue` only add. You can set `blockedBy` on a new issue whose blockers already exist. To drop a relation, use `removeBlockedBy`, `removeBlocks`, or `removeRelatedTo`.
- **Edit a long description**: pass `patch`, a list of operations, in place of `description`. Each operation has an `op`: `replace`, `insert_before`, `insert_after`, `prepend`, `append`, or `replace_range`. An insert takes an `anchor` (text that must appear once in the description) and the `text` to add. A patch keeps an edit that another session made at the same time.
- **Read an issue**: `get_issue` with the identifier. The title and description carry the requirements. Add `includeRelations: true` for the blocking edges. `fields` limits the answer to the fields you name (and `id`) and overrides `includeRelations`, so when you pass `fields`, name every field you need, for example `description`, `createdBy`, and `relations`. Call `list_comments` with `issueId` for the thread, because decisions often live only in comments.
- **List and search**: `list_issues` with `team`, and any of `state`, `label`, `assignee` (`"null"` for unassigned), `parentId`, or `query`. A list call returns one page of at most 250 items. Keep following `cursor` while `hasNextPage` is true, or older items drop out of the list. This holds for `list_issues`, `list_comments`, and `list_issue_labels`.
- **Comment**: `save_comment` with `issueId` and `body`. Pass `parentId` to reply inside a thread.
- **Labels and states**: `list_issue_labels` and `list_issue_statuses` (both take `team`) show what exists. `save_issue_label` creates a label. Its `teamId` is the team UUID from `list_teams`. Never rename or delete a label that already exists. The label `repo:cre-skills-plugin` is not one of the five triage labels, so the team may not have it yet. Check with `list_issue_labels`, and create it before the first issue that needs it.
- **Projects**: `save_project`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create an issue as described above: a plain `title`, a Markdown `description`, and `labels` that hold the triage role the skill names (see `triage-labels.md`) and `repo:cre-skills-plugin`. `to-spec` and `to-tickets` use `ready-for-agent` unless the user says otherwise. Publish the blockers before the tickets they block, so that each ticket can name real identifiers.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `get_issue` with `includeRelations: true`, then `list_comments` with `issueId`. Read the whole thread before you act.

## Blocking edges and sub-issues

Use the native Linear relations. Set `blockedBy` (or `blocks`) with `save_issue` to record that one issue gates another. Set `parentId` to make an issue a sub-issue. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is in a `completed`, `canceled`, or `duplicate` state. To read the state of a blocker, call `get_issue` for it with `fields: ["statusType"]`.

## Triage labels

Use these five labels: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. `triage-labels.md` in this directory maps each role, and the two category roles `bug` and `enhancement`, to Linear labels.

- `ready-for-agent` identifies work for agents. It is the queue an autonomous session works from.
- `ready-for-human` identifies work that needs human action.
- `needs-info` identifies an open question recorded on the issue.
- Start comments from the `triage` skill with this line: `> *This was generated by AI during triage.*`
- The reporter is the creator of the issue (ask for `createdBy` in `fields`). Mention a user with `@displayName`.
- To point at a repo file such as `.out-of-scope/<concept>.md` in a comment, give its path. Build a GitHub link from `git remote get-url origin` only if a link helps.

To show what needs attention, call `list_issues` for the team with `fields` that include `labels`, `statusType`, and `createdAt`. Follow `cursor` until `hasNextPage` is false. Drop each issue whose `statusType` is `completed`, `canceled`, or `duplicate`. Make three lists of the rest, oldest first:

1. Unlabeled: issues that hold none of the five triage labels (see `triage-labels.md`) and no `wayfinder:*` label.
2. `needs-triage`: issues that hold this label.
3. `needs-info`: issues that hold this label and have a comment from the reporter that is newer than the last triage notes. Call `list_comments` with `issueId` to check.

To find the queue of `ready-for-agent`, call `list_issues` for the team with `label` set to `ready-for-agent` and `fields` that include `labels`, `statusType`, `assignee`, and `createdAt`. Follow `cursor` until `hasNextPage` is false. Drop each issue whose `statusType` is `started`, `completed`, `canceled`, or `duplicate`, and each issue that has an assignee. Keep the issues that hold `repo:cre-skills-plugin` and the issues that hold no `repo:` label. Work the oldest first, after you check its blockers as described under "Blocking edges and sub-issues". Claim it as described under "Wayfinding operations" (`assignee: "me"`), before any other work.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** `triage` works on Linear issues only. Review a GitHub pull request with `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `wayfinder`. The **map** is a parent issue. Its tickets are sub-issues of the map. On a new map or ticket, `labels` holds the `wayfinder:*` label named here and, when the work belongs to one repository alone, `repo:cre-skills-plugin`.

- **One-time setup**: the `wayfinder:*` labels are not part of the five triage labels. Before the first wayfinder run, call `list_issue_labels` for the team. Create each missing label with `save_issue_label`: `wayfinder:map`, `wayfinder:research`, `wayfinder:prototype`, `wayfinder:grilling`, `wayfinder:task`. Create only the missing ones.
- **Names and links**: refer to a ticket by its title. Wrap the title in the issue `url` (`[Title](url)`). `list_issues` and `get_issue` return `url` only when you name it in `fields`. With `get_issue`, name `relations` too, because `fields` overrides `includeRelations`.
- **Map**: create an issue with `save_issue`: `team`, a `title`, and `labels: ["wayfinder:map"]`. The description holds Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, and Out of scope, as `wayfinder` lays them out.
- **Child ticket**: create an issue with `save_issue`: `team`, a `title`, the question as `description`, `parentId` set to the map, and `labels: ["wayfinder:<research|prototype|grilling|task>"]`. Create all the tickets first. Wire the blocking edges in a second pass, because a ticket needs an identifier before another ticket can name it.
- **Blocking**: the native relation. Call `save_issue` on the blocked ticket with `blockedBy` set to the identifiers of its blockers. Linear shows the blocked state in its own UI, so the human sees the frontier without opening the map.
- **Frontier query**: find the next ticket. It is the first open, unblocked, unclaimed child of the map, in map order.
  1. Call `list_issues` with `parentId` set to the map and `fields` set to `["title", "status", "statusType", "assignee", "createdAt", "url"]`. Follow `cursor` until `hasNextPage` is false.
  2. Drop each child whose `statusType` is `completed`, `canceled`, or `duplicate`.
  3. Drop each child that has an assignee.
  4. For each child that is left, call `get_issue` with `includeRelations: true`. For each blocker it lists, call `get_issue` for the blocker with `fields: ["statusType"]`. Drop the child if one blocker has a `statusType` other than `completed`, `canceled`, or `duplicate`.
  5. Sort the rest by `createdAt`, oldest first. That is map order. The first one is next.
- **Claim**: `save_issue` with `id` and `assignee: "me"`, before any other work. The assignee is the claim.
- **Resolve**: record the answer, close the ticket, and add a pointer to the map.
  1. Call `save_comment` with the answer.
  2. Call `save_issue` with `state: "Done"`. This is the `completed` state of the team, so check `list_issue_statuses` if the name differs.
  3. Add a one-line context pointer to the map's Decisions so far. Use a `patch` operation on the map description. Its `op` is `insert_before`, and its `anchor` is the heading `## Not yet specified`. Its `text` is the new line, then a blank line: `- [Title](url): <context>` followed by two newline characters. The blank line keeps the heading on its own line.
  A `research` ticket is resolved by its subagent with these same steps. Put the pointer to its `research/<name>` branch in the resolution comment.

## Language

Use ASD-STE100 simplified technical English.
Use short active sentences and normal spaces between words.
Keep exact identifiers, commands, code, and quoted evidence unchanged.
Keep historical source text separate from current instructions.

## Skills that read this file

`to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `triage`, and `wayfinder` use this tracker configuration, with `triage-labels.md`.
Their shared discovery root is `~/.agents/skills/`.
Do not run `setup-matt-pocock-skills` in this repo. It proposes GitHub Issues and would overwrite these files.
